[i]Fantastic news! The Royal Family is welcome to stay at the palace. Attached is a brief itinerary...[/i] Began Elena's cordial return e-mail. She called the head of Palace Staff, Galina, to her office to discuss Maslenitsa accommodations. The Palace would host the family from the 20th to the morning of the 24th (Sunday - Thursday), so that they could still have their holiday at home.

The first two days (Mon/Tue, Sunday is for arrival and a quiet dinner) would be spent in attendance of the Festival Dances in Velnaz and Chernigyiv- the capitol and Bolochia's "Great Stone City", a castle town and one of the frontier fortifications of the Meiora elves. Wednesday night there would be a feast at the Palace, with music played by a string quartet.

[b]Commerce![/b]

[i]Possibly a surprise to both the Senate and the newly formed Parliament, Dushkaria has finally gotten trade deals! The current bureaucrats assigned to trade seems to be slightly overworked, as there is quite real limits to what two bureaucrats can do.[/i]

[i]And as such, the Commerce and Industry mediation Committee has been hastily founded to make trade and contracts with Dushkari industry much easier. And as such, the CIC officially welcomes [nation]Koranvistan[/nation] and [nation]Corzerran[/nation] to Dushkaria![/i]

Transitioning the millitary fully out of war time size.
[spoiler=Kuhaw-Astan Military Reforms]
While the military of Kuhaw-Astan have been heavily reduced in personnel numbers after the end of the Astanir civil war, were at the height of the conflict they reached a peak in their number of used available recruitable population of 35%, that number have now been brought down to a far more rational 10% for a nation no longer at war.
While most of the tribal senate agree that this number needs to be further reduced, it has been hotly debated the last year or so just how much lower and what manner of military should be pursued in peace time for it to be able to defend the nation from potential threats, by the 14th of February an agreement was finally reached and agreed upon by all parties of how the size and maintaining of the military should be.

Its size were to be set up as such;
Standing army at 2.5%, fully dedicated military personnel.
Reserve soldiers at 2.5%, will have regular training and exercises but will otherwise be able to hold civilian jobs.
National Guard at 2%, less regular training and exercises, to be used for emergencies, disasters and lesser military duties, but will have a less interrupted civilian life.

This will allow the military to quickly deploy 5-7% of the population in the case of war but will have far less economic and social impact then a 5% standing army and as such adequately satisfies all concerns of the multiple tribes of Kuhaw-Astan.

A greater focus on quality is also to be adopted and the military command will be tasked to start finding suppliers of military weapons, vehicles and equipment for all branches of the military to start a slow but steady upgrade of the military's inventory for future defence where especially the navy and air defence is to be given priority as they are the most in need of modernizing to meet the needs and threats of modern warfare.

This work to implement this reform is to be started immediately, signed by President Pemuluwuy Nuru-Lukywa and the tribal senate.
[/spoiler]

[list]──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[b]Parliament approved and sanctioned the establishment of diplomatic relations with [nation=noflag]Koranvistan[/nation].
[sub]Le Parlement a approuvé et sanctionné l'établissement de relations diplomatiques avec le [nation=noflag]Koranvistan[/nation].[/b][/sub]
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────[/list]

[i][b]P A R L I A M E N T / P A R L E M E N T ─[/b][/i] On February 18, following a parliamentary vote, the Pirn Parliament officially approved the establishment of diplomatic relations with [nation=noflag]Koranvistan[/nation], a northern nation. The decision is widely seen as a major milestone in Pirns history, marking the first time the country has formed diplomatic ties with another state since gaining independence in 1955. The move has sparked excitement among citizens, while members of Parliament and the Government also expressed strong satisfaction. According to President [i][b]Ariana Doolan[/b][/i], [i]The Parliaments approval shows a shift from maintaining Pirn as a nation open to tourists but closed to diplomacy, toward full integration. This will be a crucial step as our country joins the international and global community.[/i]

Public reaction has been overwhelmingly positive, with many citizens saying they are thrilled to see Parliament finally take action toward international integration rather than limiting foreign interaction to tourism. [i]I feel like Ive become a global citizen![/i] one resident told journalist [b][i]Patrick Nicholson[/i][/b]. Meanwhile, the government of [i][b]Jackson Rearden[/b][/i] has begun preparations for an official visit to [nation=noflag]Koranvistan[/nation] to sign and formalize diplomatic relations. [i]Its time for us to engage more with the world,[/i] diplomat [i][b]Célestine Pelletier[/b][/i] said. [i]We need to climb out of the well we built for ourselves, we cant stay inside it forever thinking the world is only what we see from below.[/i]

However, despite strong support from the public and government, opposition lawmakers, most prominently the political organization [b]Advanced Red Coalition (ARC)[/b], continue to reject the move. According to party member [i][b]Winona Bacchus[/b][/i], [i]International integration at this moment is far too dangerous and risky. We have no way of knowing what those people intend for our country. Parliament agreed far too hastily and without caution. This is unacceptable, and the vote was clearly influenced.[/i] Her remarks were widely criticized by experts as conservative and extreme, lacking evidence and ultimately drawing even more backlash from both the public and political circles. [i]Shes clearly been hypnotized by fear![/i] wrote [i][b]Austin Goodwin[/b][/i], a member of the [b]Future Vision Party[/b], on the social platform [i]PirnYouthToday[/i].

Pirns youth have also expressed great enthusiasm. Many say they have long dreamed of studying abroad, working overseas, or simply traveling, but were unable to do so because the government allowed foreigners in while restricting its own citizens from leaving. Now, they feel a new era is opening. [i]Parliament has done exactly what our founding father Thomas Lavery once said: Parliament was born to serve the people, the loyal servant of the people, serving and bringing joy to the people. And today, the people are joyful![/i] said [i][b]Camelia Maxwell[/b][/i], a student at [i]Bélême University of Technical and Technological Education[/i].

[b]An earthquake struck the southern part of Lisdoran Island, causing numerous deaths, injuries, and extensive damage.
[sub]Un tremblement de terre a frappé la partie sud de l'île de Lisdoran, provoquant de nombreux morts, des blessés et d'importants dégâts.[/b][/sub]
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────[/list]

At [b]7:32 p.m.[/b] [i](local time)[/i] on February 17, a powerful 5.9-magnitude earthquake struck [b]Westway Commune[/b] in [b]Newlip District[/b], [b]Rosgheda Province[/b], marking the first recorded earthquake in the history of Pirn. With no previous seismic events and no warning systems in place, local authorities were unable to alert residents in time, leaving many unprepared to evacuate. The disaster caused heavy casualties and extensive destruction, with economic losses estimated at 700 million Potoca.

According to the [b][i]Westway Newspaper[/i][/b], nearly 229 residents across 15 hamlets were killed, while 542 others were injured. The tragedy has shocked the nation as well as government officials. Neighboring provinces, [b]Lisford, Nelarney, Limegal[/b], and [b]Diçon[/b], have mobilized rescue teams to assist [b]Rosgheda[/b]. The national government has called on citizens to donate and volunteer alongside emergency crews in the affected area. Geological experts have also been dispatched to monitor the region and provide early-warning assessments in case of aftershocks or future seismic activity.

The earthquake is now regarded as the most devastating natural disaster ever recorded in Pirn, as the country had no history of such events. In response, Parliament convened an emergency session and passed the [i][b]Natural Hazard Alert Act[/b][/i], mandating the creation of seismic monitoring stations, public education on earthquake preparedness, and the development of mobile-based early-warning systems.
